newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business inventories up in April.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business inventories up in April.

text.p: Weaker U.S. retail sales helped drive inventories held by businesses up in April, the Commerce Department said on Friday, adding to signs of a slower pace of business activity as spring began.

Total business inventories rose 0.3 percent in April to a seasonally adjusted $1.02 trillion after a revised 0.2 percent increase in March. Previously, the department said inventories rose 0.3 percent in March.
Wall Street economists had forecast April inventories would rise by 0.2 percent.
Total business sales rose in April by 0.3 percent to $746.34 billion following a revised 0.2 percent fall in March that previously was reported as a 0.3 percent decline.
The biggest change in inventories during April occurred at the retail level, where stocks of unsold goods climbed 0.8 percent to $317.89 billion after shrinking by 0.2 percent in April.
Manufacturers' inventories were up 0.6 percent to $445.68 billion in April following a 0.2 percent rise in March.
By contrast, wholesalers' inventories dropped in April by 0.7 percent to 257.64 billion after a 0.5 percent increase in March.
On the sales side, retailers' sales were down sharply by 0.9 percent to $210.52 billion after a 0.3 percent fall in March.

On Thursday, the department said sales by retail stores dropped for a third straight month in May. That, along with the latest report of mounting retail inventories, adds to the impression of a sharp economic slowdown in the second quarter.
Sales by manufacturers posted a strong 1.2 percent increase to 325.63 billion following a 0.1 percent gain in March.
Wholesalers' sales were unchanged in April at $210.19 billion after declining 0.8 percent in March.
The inventory-to-sales ratio -- a measure of how long it would take to sell existing stocks at the current pace -- was unchanged in April at 1.37 months' worth.
